Full pairwise correlation table

Source: R/dsc.R
cortbl.Rd

Computes the correlation of every pair of numeric columns and returns it in long form – one row per pair, which is easier to sort, filter and join than a matrix – with the number of complete pairs each figure rests on.

Usage

cortbl(data, mthd = c("spearman", "pearson"), minprs = 3L)

# S3 method for class 'cortbl'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame; its numeric columns are correlated in pairs.

mthd

"spearman" (default) or "pearson".

minprs

Minimum complete pairs required before a correlation is computed, a whole number of at least 2 (default 3). Below it the pair is NA rather than a number computed from almost nothing.

x

A result of cortbl().

...

Not used.

Value

A data frame of class c("cortbl", "data.frame") with one row per pair of numeric columns and the columns x and y (character, the column names), correlation (numeric, in \([-1, 1]\) or NA) and nprs (integer); the method is in attr(, "method").

Details

Non-numeric columns are ignored. For each pair, rows where either value is missing are dropped (pairwise deletion), so different pairs can rest on different rows; nprs says how many. Spearman's rank correlation (the default) is the Pearson correlation of the ranks, robust to outliers and to monotone transformations; see topcors for why it is the default. A pair with fewer than minprs complete rows, or with a constant column (no variance), gets NA. The pairs are listed in column order (utils::combn()).

Errors: data not a data frame; fewer than two numeric columns; minprs not a whole number of at least 2; an invalid mthd.

See also

topcors for just the strongest.

Examples

set.seed(1)
df <- data.frame(a = stats::rnorm(100), b = stats::rnorm(100))
df$c <- df$a + stats::rnorm(100, sd = 0.2) # simulated

cortbl(df)
#> Correlations (spearman): 3 pairs
#>  x y correlation nprs
#>  a b      0.0387  100
#>  a c      0.9665  100
#>  b c      0.0151  100

# Pearson instead of Spearman
cortbl(df, mthd = "pearson")
#> Correlations (pearson): 3 pairs
#>  x y correlation nprs
#>  a b   -0.000994  100
#>  a c    0.974707  100
#>  b c   -0.012038  100

# nprs shows how much data each figure rests on.
gappy <- df
gappy$a[1:80] <- NA
cortbl(gappy)
#> Correlations (spearman): 3 pairs
#>  x y correlation nprs
#>  a b      0.1654   20
#>  a c      0.9594   20
#>  b c      0.0151  100

# A pair with too little overlap is NA, not a number from nothing.
thin <- df
thin$a[1:99] <- NA
cortbl(thin)$correlation
#> [1]         NA         NA 0.01508551

# one numeric column cannot be correlated
try(cortbl(data.frame(a = 1:5, b = letters[1:5])))
#> Error : cortbl: need at least two numeric columns to correlate.
